subject: POC Access MAP — pre-close environment runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + MAP to get POC environment provisioned

Hi Alice — great to meet you on the demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to move fast on a short MAP (mutual action plan) so your engineering team can validate latency and billing profiles in a constrained POC. Vanessa (our AE) will coordinate the close timeline and ops steps.

High level ask from Acme: test inference across a 2-week evaluation using your clinical routing workload. To get you into a POC environment we typically need: 1) org/team setup in our console, 2) API key(s) scoped to the trial project, 3) source IP allowlist for the testing runners, and 4) optional VPC peering for higher throughput tests.

Vanessa — can you propose a two-week runbook and handoff sequence? Ill loop in Marissa for credentialing.

Next steps: Vanessa to send a MAP doc + timeline; Alice to confirm which network option (allowlist vs peering).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intro + MAP to get POC environment provisioned

Hi Ben/Vanessa — thanks, this aligns with what we want. A couple of clarifying items before you send the formal MAP: 

- Org setup: will we be added to your console as a single org with project-level isolation, or do you create a separate org per customer? We need to clarify access boundaries for our audit team.
- API keys: we prefer short-lived keys for the POC and a rollout path to managed service account tokens. Can you outline the key rotation cadence?
- IP allowlist: we can supply a handful of egress IPs from our cloud test runners. If we opt for VPC peering, well need an architecture diagram and peering window (preferred weekend).
- Timeline: target start for the POC is Sep 7 (two weeks after next Tue). Are you able to commit resources to meet that window?

If you can attach a simple MAP with explicit owner-by-day items and any compliance artifacts (SOC2 or data-binding notes), well route internally.

—Alice
Alice Moreno
Senior Product Manager, Integrations
Acme Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: POC MAP (draft) — owners, timeline, and ops runbook

Alice — attaching a concise MAP (POC_MAP_v1.pdf) and a network sketch (network_diagram_v2.png). Below is the runbook in-line for quick review. If that looks good, well lock owners and calendar invites.

POC MAP (summary) — 2-week evaluation starting Sep 7 (target)
Week 0 — Preflight (owner: Vanessa / Marissa)
  • Create Acme org in Redwood console, set project = acme-poc (Vanessa)
  • Provision two scoped API keys: poc-read and poc-infer (Marissa) — keys are 7-day TTL by default; rotation notes included in attachment
  • Receive IP allowlist from Acme OR schedule VPC peering window (Neha to coordinate peering window with infra)
  • Provide SOC2 and minimal data flow note (attachment)
Week 1 — Ramp + validation (owner: Acme + Marissa)
  • Run baseline throughput test (Acme)
  • Telemetry hooks enabled (Marissa) — token-level usage and latency dashboards shared
  • If peering: establish route table and test connectivity in a maintenance window
Week 2 — Close + handoff
  • Execute acceptance tests, capture perf/quality metrics (joint)
  • Discuss next-step commitment (Dedicated or Hosted billing)

Operational notes:
  - API keys: default TTL 7 days for POC; support for rotating via API and for exchanging to service-account tokens after acceptance. See attachment section 2.
  - IP allowlist: we support CIDR entries and single IPs. For rapid start provide up to 8 egress IPs and well add them to the trial runner ACL.
  - VPC peering: requires an infra ticket and a peering CIDR confirmation. Typical peering turnaround is 48–72 hours once both sides approve. Weekend peering (Sat-Sun) recommended for minimal disruption.

Attachments: POC_MAP_v1.pdf (detailed owners and deadlines), network_diagram_v2.png (peering sketch).

Please confirm: 1) POC start (Sep 7) OK? 2) Will you provide allowlist IPs or request peering? 3) Any compliance blockers (we can redact logs and use redwoods private deployment checklist if needed).

If helpful I can propose calendar blocks for the Preflight and Peering window.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, West
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: POC MAP (draft) — owners, timeline, and ops runbook

Vanessa — quick runbook notes from credentialing/network side. Quoting your timelines for context.

On 2026-08-24 Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> POC MAP (summary) — 2-week evaluation starting Sep 7 (target)

Internal checklist items: 
  1) I will generate the two scoped API keys on Aug 31 and place them in the secure share for Acme. Keys will be 7-day TTL; if you need continuous access during the POC we can issue a rolling key on day 8.
  2) IP allowlist format: please send as CSV with columns: name, ip, cidr, owner-email. Ill import directly to the trial ACL.
  3) VPC peering: Neha, can you confirm our preferred peering window? Acme prefers weekend; we have an availability slot Sep 11-12. If Acme opts for peering well request their VPC details by Sep 1 to meet that window.

Neha — pinging you for peering capacity and any additional infra tickets we should open ahead of time.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC MAP (draft) — owners, timeline, and ops runbook

Thanks — this is helpful and the Sep 7 start looks good on our side. Quick confirmations: 
  • We will start with IP allowlist for the initial ramp. Our DevSecOps team will send the CSV (name,ip,cidr,owner-email) by Aug 28.
  • If needed we will request peering; please tentatively hold Sep 11-12 as a possible peering window.
  • API keys: 7-day TTL is fine for now. Well request a rolling key on day 8 if we continue.
  • Compliance: Acme requires the SOC2 summary (just the control coverage) — if you can attach that to the MAP we can expedite internal review.

I approve the MAP as draft — please lock owners and send calendar invites for the Preflight (Aug 31) and Week 1 sync (Sep 14).

Best,
